question.text: Which of the following is NOT classified as a 'material change' to the PPM that triggers compulsory exit option for investors under SEBI (AIF) Regulations?

answer.text: Change in sponsor or manager of the AIF (not including internal restructuring within the group)
Change in control of the sponsor or manager of the AIF
Change in fee structure or hurdle rate that may adversely affect investors
Change in the address, email ID, or contact number of the AIF's Manager or Sponsor

explanation.text: The Logic: Per Section 13.5.3, material changes include (1) change in sponsor/manager (excluding internal group restructuring), (2) change in control of sponsor/manager, and (3) change in fee structure or hurdle rate that may adversely affect investors. Per Annexure 13.1 Section 5, non-material changes include bank account, address, email ID, and contact number — these do NOT require investor vote or exit option. The Trap: Contact/address changes feel important but are administratively non-material. The classification matters because material changes require consolidated investor intimation and compulsory exit rights. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-A tests the list of material changes at recall level. XIX-C tests the non-material counterpart and the procedural exit-right mechanism. Manager's Pro-Tip: When proposing any PPM change, run a 'materiality check' with legal counsel first. Structuring a change as non-material (e.g., strategy tweak worded as clarification rather than change) can save you an expensive compulsory-exit event.
